description: A materials manager must decide how to release and route 900 recovered stainless-steel blanks for two open production orders, finalizing the disposition, press assignment, staging, inspection, and residue-handling controls.

shared_context.S1: A recovered lot of 900 stainless-steel blanks is available after a cancelled production order, and two current customer orders can use the blanks.
shared_context.S2: The normal practice is to prioritize the older customer order when recovered material is released.
shared_context.S3: The blanks have not yet been released to production, and the materials manager's signed disposition is required before they can be moved into the work area.
shared_context.S4: At the disposition meeting, the materials manager follows the plant's routine practice of taking a report from quality, process engineering, logistics, and environmental health and safety before signing the release.

PF1.text: Jonas's hardness and surface review found that exactly 720 blanks meet the material specification and exactly 180 blanks have decarburized surfaces; quality requires the 720 conforming blanks to receive 100% visual inspection and the 180 nonconforming blanks to be quarantined. He completed the review this morning, but the disposition record has not yet been attached to the lot.

PF2.text: Priya's forming trial found that only Press 4 with fixture F-12 can process these recovered blanks without edge cracking; changing Press 4 to fixture F-12 requires exactly 75 minutes of setup. She ran the trial during yesterday's engineering check, but the result is still in her offline trial notebook.

PF3.text: Luis's bin reconciliation shows that the 720 conforming blanks must be staged in bins B31 through B35 and the 180 quarantined blanks must remain isolated in bin B36; the current warehouse labels still show the old cancelled-order status.

PF4.text: Nadia's EHS review classified the residual forming oil on this recovered lot as solvent-contaminated material, requiring washing in Bay 2 before pressing and collection in exactly 4 labeled waste drums; she received the solvent classification from the waste contractor this week, but the waste-control register has not yet been updated.

acceptance_conditions: Exactly 720 blanks must be released and exactly 180 blanks must be quarantined.
The released blanks must be routed to Press 4 using fixture F-12 with exactly 75 minutes of setup.
All released blanks must receive 100% visual inspection.
The released blanks must be staged in bins B31 through B35 and the quarantined blanks must remain isolated in bin B36.
The blanks must be washed in Bay 2 before pressing and the residue must be collected in exactly 4 labeled waste drums.
The quality review must be cited as justification.

decisive_facts.why: The review changes the disposition from treating all 900 blanks alike to releasing exactly 720, quarantining exactly 180, and applying 100% visual inspection to the released quantity.
The forming trial changes the route to Press 4 with fixture F-12 and fixes the setup duration at exactly 75 minutes.
The bin reconciliation changes the staging assignments to B31 through B35 for the released blanks and isolated bin B36 for the quarantined blanks.
The solvent classification changes handling to washing in Bay 2 and fixes residue collection at exactly 4 labeled waste drums.
